scope: Standing 1907 masonry bridge crossing 4 along the west shore of the Tai Tam Tuk Reservoir. Includes masonry arches, tapered pier supports, cornice, parapets and the mapped road approach.
geometryBasis: Separate official historic-boundary polygon 948 and native OpenStreetMap bridge way 328552506 agree about the road alignment. Each bridge is independently placed on its own ground.
sectionBasis: Granite-faced masonry arch ring, tapered piers, horizontal cornice, stone parapet and footway. Original terrain locates the ravine and the approaches.
limitations: The heritage boundary and road trace establish the location and plan. Exact pier stations, spring heights, parapets and visible foundations are estimates.
A written first-person description records six exposed arches immediately downstream of the Intermediate Reservoir. Their individual widths are estimated.

The 5 m elevation grid represents original surveyed ground and the reservoir surface. Submerged foundations and channel depths are outside the available data. Near-deck apparent sculpting in the elevation model is kept in the preview.

facts.basis: first-person written observation of the exposed bridge
